canonical_question: How do I choose between track Flex mode and region Flex & Follow for enabling Flex Time at track and region scope?
clarification_questions: Is the entire phrase late, one event late, or is the project tempo/grid itself the wrong reference?
What source is this, which Flex mode and Flex & Follow setting are active, and is the audio dry, stereo, grouped, or multitrack?
What exactly became wrong after the edit: pitch, attack, sustain, ambience, stereo image, phase, neighboring timing, or musical feel?

direct_answer: Flex availability, the selected Flex algorithm, and each region’s Flex & Follow state are separate decisions. Verify scope before diagnosing timing. Track flex mode and region Flex & Follow solve different timing scopes; compare them on the same event.
evidence_needed: The current Logic version, source type, mono/stereo or multimic scope, Flex mode, Flex & Follow setting, Smart Tempo mode, markers, and group state.
The untouched baseline plus the exact event before, during, and after the timing edit.
Current transient-marker and flex-marker placement, and whether audio quantization or Smart Tempo is also active.
The user’s report of timing improvement, artifacts, groove, emotion, attack, pitch, ambience, phase, and adjacent-material changes.
key_distinction: Flex availability, the selected Flex algorithm, and each region’s Flex & Follow state are separate decisions. Verify scope before diagnosing timing.
limitations: Timing appearance on a grid does not prove musical improvement.
Flex algorithms and artifacts depend on source type, amount, ambience, stereo/multimic relationships, and current Logic behavior.
Professional/community sources are context-bound and may disagree.
Exact Logic procedures remain unverified on the owner’s installed build.

logic_guidance.listen_for: only the intended region becoming editable and following the desired timing reference
logic_guidance.location: Logic Tracks area > Show Flex > track Flex mode; Region inspector > Flex & Follow
logic_guidance.risk: Enabling broader tempo-follow behavior can move more material than the user intended.
logic_guidance.show_me_query: Logic Tracks area > Show Flex > track Flex mode; Region inspector > Flex & Follow
logic_guidance.starting_point: Begin with the selected region and Flex & Follow On rather than Bars/Beats unless tempo conformance is intended.
steps: Save a Track/Project Alternative or duplicate the region, and document the current Flex mode, Flex & Follow state, tempo mode, markers, quantization, and group settings.
Create two preserved alternatives: one using track Flex mode and one using region Flex & Follow. Use the same event and change nothing else.
Replay at least one musical event before and after the target, then compare against the untouched baseline in the full arrangement.
Listen for: only the intended region becoming editable and following the desired timing reference.
Stop or back off if: Enabling broader tempo-follow behavior can move more material than the user intended.
Turn Flex/Flex & Follow back to its documented prior state and restore the duplicated region.
logic_guidance.stop_condition: Stop once the distracting timing problem is no longer audible in context and the result meets this listening target: only the intended region becoming editable and following the desired timing reference. Back off or undo if Enabling broader tempo-follow behavior can move more material than the user intended.
logic_guidance.undo: Turn Flex/Flex & Follow back to its documented prior state and restore the duplicated region.
logic_guidance.version_scope: Logic Pro 12.3 target; verify exact labels, modes, marker behavior, Smart Tempo settings, quantization parameters, and group controls against the installed version.
logic_guidance.visual_target_query: Logic Tracks area > Show Flex > track Flex mode; Region inspector > Flex & Follow

non_processing_possibilities: Move the complete region, slice/crossfade, choose another take, re-record, or let the project tempo follow the performance when those better preserve the source.
problem_summary: Flex seems enabled but the region does not behave as expected
recommended_first_experiment: Create two preserved alternatives: one using track Flex mode and one using region Flex & Follow. Use the same event and change nothing else.
teaching_principle: Flex availability, the selected Flex algorithm, and each region’s Flex & Follow state are separate decisions. Verify scope before diagnosing timing.
title: Enabling Flex Time At Track And Region Scope — compare
tradeoffs: The edit can improve only the intended region becoming editable and following the desired timing reference, but Enabling broader tempo-follow behavior can move more material than the user intended.
A visually tighter result can sound less musical.
A local timing improvement can redistribute stretch or phase damage to neighboring material.
user_intent: Choose between two commonly confused timing approaches.
